Paramount Pictures and Danny McBride are putting up their Duke.
Bradley Cooper has signed on for military duty to star in Paramount’s new and untitled G.I. Joe feature.
McBride, known primarily as an actor and for his work as creator of HBO’s The Righteous Gemstones, is directing the project. He also wrote the script, along with Jeff Fradley and John Carcieri.

Little is known about the new take on the Hasbro property, a toy line that gained its modern relevance from a relaunch that included a cartoon series and a Marvel Comics comic in the 1980s. (It was first launched in mid-1960s as a realistic soldier toy.)

It was this version that not only introduced a commando strike force featuring soldiers with monikers such as Duke, Roadblock and Snake Eyes but also its over-the-top, hi-tech adversary, the terrorist organization known as Cobra, with key bad guys including Cobra Commander, Baroness, Destro and Zartan.

Cooper will play Duke, the nominal leader of the Joes. The character was played by Channing Tatum in the live-action movies G.I. Joe: Rise of Cobra and G.I. Joe: Retaliation, released by Paramount in 2009 and 2013, respectively.

The Joe feature has been one of the big priorities at the studio, which, under new owner David Ellison, has been ramping up development of major IP and brands such as Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and Star Trek. Securing Cooper as the lead of what will be an ensemble signals that, among the IP plays, the project may be the one that gets before cameras and presumably theaters first.
Producing are Lorenzo di Bonaventura, Mark Vahradian and Zev Foreman of Hasbro Entertainment.

G.I. Joe is a rare IP play for Cooper, whose last major role was starring as Leonard Bernstein in Maestro, the ambitious biopic he also co-wrote and directed, earning four Oscar nominations in the process.

Cooper is known as the voice of Rocket in Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy movies and had a cameo in James Gunn’s Superman movie last year. He worked with McBride previously when he appeared in episode of Gemstones.

Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos is breaking down why he thinks his streamer lost Stranger Things creators The Duffer Bros. and the hit show’s executive producer and director Shawn Levy to rival studios.

Matt and Ross Duffer surprised the industry by announcing they were jumping ship to Paramount last August in a four-year exclusive deal that covered film and TV. They officially made the switch in April.

Then Levy, who is directing the upcoming Star Wars: Starfighter for Lucasfilm, was announced as leaving for Disney’s 20th Television after a decade spent at Netflix. His deal via his 21 Laps Entertainment production company beings next October.
The Hollywood Reporter asked Sarandos about the high-profile defections of three men who were responsible for what’s arguably the streamer’s biggest hit series.

“The Duffers have worked with us for [a] decade and did not want to make more TV shows right now,” Sarandos said. “They really want to make big tentpole theatrical movies. And I said to Matt and Ross, ‘You guys are great at what you do, and I think you should go do that. You’re 40. Don’t wake up when you’re 60 wishing you did that 20 years later.’ And I’m thrilled for them. They’re going to have great success.”

Sarandos pointed out that Netflix still owns the Stranger Things franchise, which could have still some additional content to come. “We — the Stranger Things universe — are going to continue to be a part of [that success] forever,” he added.
As for Levy, Sarandos suggested the director likewise wanted to make major theatrical films — and suggested that Levy will make more Star Wars movies after Starfighter is released next year.

“Shawn also was kind of doing the same thing. And the problem when you have an overall deal with someone who has commitments in other places, you’re in constant conflict for their time. And Shawn is going to be making Star Wars movies for a while. So the fact that his deal is with Disney makes a lot of sense. I’m thrilled for Shawn. We’re going to do a ton of things together.”
Sarandos added Netflix still has shows in development with Levy, including an upcoming hockey drama titled Sticks. “We have a lot of that stuff’s going to stick around,” he said.

The Duffer Brothers have similarly explained that movies were their reason for leaving Netflix, with Matt Duffer saying, “The biggest draw to us was just to be able to do something theatrical, which is not something Netflix does.”
Levy’s statement about his Disney deal was more vague, saying he has “always felt a kindred spirit in Disney and their storytelling ethos” and noting the studio “feels like home.”
Talia Ryder is the latest star lacing up their dance shoes for Tom Holland’s Fred Astaire biopic.

The Sony production about the legendary dancer and actor of Hollywood’s Golden Age has already tapped Margaret Qualley to play Adele Astaire, Fred’s older sister and Broadway partner, and Sabrina Carpenter as Ginger Rogers, Fred Astaire’s frequent film co-star. Ryder, a classically trained dancer, will play June Allyson, a dancer and MGM actress who was originally set to star opposite Astaire in the musical film Royal Wedding.
Paddington filmmaker Paul King is directing from a screenplay he wrote with Steven Levenson based on the book The Astaires: Fred & Adele by Kathleen Riley.

Amy Pascal and Rachel O’Connor produce for Pascal Pictures along with Ben Holden and Josh Hyams for Lightbulb Pictures and Holland for Billy17. Steven Levenson and King penned the script based on the book The Astaires: Fred & Adele by Kathleen Riley.
The film has support from some Astaire family members, including Fred’s daughter, Ava Astaire McKenzie. Her son, Tyler McKenzie, serves as a consultant and co-producer.

Ryder‘s onscreen credits include a breakout in Sundance indie Never Rarely Sometimes Always and Ethan Coen’s Honey Don’t, where she appeared opposite Qualley. As for musical cred, Ryder had a role in Steven Speilberg’s adaptation of West Side Story and began her career in Broadway‘s Matilda the Musical.
Ryder, who is repped by UTA, LBI and Vainshtein Law, will next be seen in Amazon MGM’s 4 Kids Walk Into A Bank and the second season of Amazon Prime’s Mr. & Mrs. Smith.
Bruno Mars may have just found the perfect way to get Karol G back.

Just days after joking that he needed to “get” the Colombian superstar back from Drake, Mars has recruited Karol G for the new music video for his lovely The Romantic track “Dance With Me,” released Thursday (Oct. 1).

The video opens with Mars strumming an electric guitar all by his lonesome, pleading the lyrics into a pay phone. Karol is on the other line, sulking in bed in a lace outfit. Mars moves on from the telephone booth to where Karol resides, serenading her from below her balcony with a full band behind him. It’s a dreamy, old-fashioned serenade, with Mars singing to Karol as the instruments flourish. Karol makes her way below, jumping into Mars’ arms as fireworks explode in the sky. The duo stares into each other’s eyes as the video comes to a close, ending the night on a wholesome — and, quite literally, a romantic — note.
It’s a fitting visual for “Dance With Me,” which finds Mars leaning into the kind of swooning romance that has become a signature theme within his discography.

And Karol G’s appearance comes at a bit of a funny time in their ongoing musical friendship. On Monday (Sept. 28), Mars reacted to a viral video of Drake dancing with Karol G during the rapper’s surprise appearance at her Houston concert. Posting a photo of himself staring dramatically out of the window of a private jet, Mars jokingly wrote, “I have to get her back! I must get her back! I will get her back!”

Mars and Karol G already have some musical history together, as the pair teamed up on “Still,” an all-English-synth-pop ballad from Karol G’s sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. The collaboration reached No. 41 on the Billboard Hot 100, while the album debuted at No. 8 on the Billboard 200.
They also took “Still” to the stage together for the first time when Mars surprised fans during Karol G’s Aug. 15 concert at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium.

For Mars, “Dance With Me” is the closing track on The Romantic, his first solo album in nearly a decade. The album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, while “Dance With Me” opened at No. 42 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Pophouse Entertainment said on Thursday (Oct. 1) it acquired a 50% stake of Australian singer-songwriter Sia’s publishing and master music rights, according to a joint statement from the artist and Swedish entertainment company that owns rights to music by KISS, Cyndi Lauper, Iron Maiden and Tina Turner.

“I’m really excited to be working with Pophouse,” the “Elastic Heart” artist said in the statement. “These songs mean so much to me, and I love that they really understand that and want to take care of them. I’ve been making music for a very long time now, and it feels exciting to think about all the new and different ways these songs might get to live on and find people. I’m really looking forward to seeing what we can dream up together.”

Sia and Pophouse declined to disclose terms of the deal, which included her Billboard Hot 100 chart topper “Cheap Thrills,” which features Sean Paul. TMZ reported the artist will receive $165 million for rights to the songs she wrote before 2022, with an additional $15 million for songs written after 2022 that will be held in escrow, according to its story on Tuesday (Sept. 29).

Born Sia Furler, the pop star gained acclaim for her contributions to hits like Rihanna‘s “Diamonds” and Beyoncé‘s “Pretty Hurts.” The pop star’s unmistakable voice rose to international prominence following the release of her 2014 album 1000 Forms of Fear and its Top 10 hit “Chandelier.”

Pophouse acquired Sia’s catalog with its Pophouse Fund I, which it closed with $1.3 billion in 2025 and tapped to fund the acquisition of rights to songs by KISS, Cyndi Lauper, Avicii and Swedish House Mafia.

“Sia is an artist whose extraordinary catalog and unique creative identity offer exceptional opportunities to celebrate and build on her remarkable body of work,” Pophouse CEO Jessica Koravos said in the statement. “This partnership will further empower Sia with strategic support and creative resources to continue pursuing her artistic ambitions while preserving and expanding her influence.”

Sia continues to make music, releasing “Awake Tonight” in April with Afrojack and David Guetta 15 years after the trio’s hit “Titanium.” Another Sia-Guetta collaboration, “Beautiful People” topped Spotify’s Australian Music Global Impact List in February. The chart ranks the most globally streamed songs by Australian artists.

The transaction follows what the artist has publicly called the “difficult year” defined by her bitter divorce with ex-David Bernhad and custody settlement requiring her to pay $42,500 according to month in child support.

Anthony Anderson is set to host the 2026 Soul Train Awards, airing Friday, Nov. 27, at 8 p.m. ET/PT on BET and CBS. This is the first Soul Train Awards since 2023 and the first ever to air on CBS. The two-hour show will tape on Thursday, Nov. 5, at Harris Theater in Chicago.

“I’m thrilled to be back with BET and especially excited to host Soul Train Awards in Chicago, where the Soul Train legacy began,” Anderson said in a statement. “Soul Train is more than a television show or an awards franchise; it’s a piece of our cultural history. Don Cornelius created a platform that gave Black artists a place to shine, and generations later, that spirit is still alive. I’m looking forward to celebrating the legends, the artists shaping R&B and soul today, and bringing a whole lot of fun to the night.”

Anderson, best known for his role on ABC’s long-running Black-ish, previously hosted the Soul Train Awards in 2013. The actor-comedian has an extensive resume as an awards show host. He hosted the NAACP Image Awards for nine consecutive years (2014-22) and the 75th Annual Primetime Emmy Awards in 2024. He cohosted the BET Awards in 2015 and 2016 with his Black-ish costar Tracee Ellis Ross.

“Anthony brings an incredible combination of comedic instinct, musical knowledge and genuine love for this culture,” said Connie Orlando, evp of specials, music programming and music strategy for BET. “His longstanding relationship with BET, coupled with his experience hosting some of television’s biggest award shows, makes him a natural fit for this new chapter of Soul Train Awards.”

“Anthony Anderson is an exceptional entertainer with a genuine connection to BET and the culture that Soul Train represents,” said Louis Carr, president of BET. “He understands the legacy, the music and the importance of creating a moment that brings people together. As we return Soul Train Awards to Chicago, the birthplace of the franchise, we’re excited to have Anthony at the center of this celebration.”

For his work on Black-ish, Anderson received seven consecutive Primetime Emmy nominations for outstanding lead actor in a comedy series (2015-21), four Primetime Emmy nominations for outstanding comedy series as an executive producer, three Golden Globe nominations and three Critics’ Choice nominations. He has won eight Image Awards and received six BET Award nominations.
